triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: All seven rules started at 2025-08-07, three months before Annex II inserted heading 9903.02.82, so the module applied a heading that did not yet exist to entries from 2025-08-07 through 2025-11-13 — the opposite direction of error from its siblings, and overlapping the still-operative predecessor 9903.02.58.
triage.triage_notes: Distinct from the other successor modules: this one was too early (2025-08-07), not too late (2026-02-15), which is why the commit calls it a 'premature' start; pre-fix it overlapped heading 9903.02.58's own window for that span. Source verified: same Annex II insertion of 9903.02.82-9903.02.91 effective November 14, 2025 (see index 3 notes). Companion test dates moved with it (test file, not this module file). No formula change; summary, corpus_citation_paths and two effective_period atoms per rule added.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff flips `effective_from` from '2025-08-07' to '2025-11-14' on the version of all seven rules in the ch-82 module, which is a version-window change and therefore meaning-bearing, not bookkeeping. I resolved the cited source through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, corpus commit d9d6fba): Annex II of 90 FR 59281 (FR Doc 2025-23316) states "Effective with respect to goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after 12:01 a.m. eastern time on November 14, 2025 ... 1. Headings 9903.02.36 and 9903.02.58 are hereby terminated ... 7. New headings 9903.02.82-9903.02.91 shall be inserted in numerical sequence", so heading 9903.02.82 did not exist before 2025-11-14 and the pre-fix start date disagreed with the source by three months while the predecessor .58 was still operative (terminated 2025-11-13 in the sibling diff). I could not refute the kind: nothing else in the diff changes a number, a comparison, a clause, a scope, or boolean logic — the added proof atoms, `corpus_citation_paths`, and summary sentence are provenance/metadata that merely document the date change.
triage.verifier_notes: Verification path: bundle module_files[8].diff_file plus resolve_provision.py on us/rulemaking/federal-register/2025-12-18/2025-23316 at rulespec commit 4d2856a958 (release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union, pages 59281-59317, matching the "90 Fed. Reg. 59281" cite). Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "mechanical/provenance only" — false, seven version windows move; (2) "new coverage the module never claimed" — false, the module already declared versions with the wrong start; (3) "retroactive to 2025-08-07 like Japan" — the Swiss/Liechtenstein notice contains no Aug 7 applicability; it applies Annex II from Nov 14, 2025 and directs CBP refunds for duties already collected, so the Aug 7 start had no source basis (the EO 2025-17389 Japan retroactivity is asserted in the commit body only and I did not verify it; it concerns 9903.02.72/.73, not .82). Caveat for a reviewer: 4d2856a958 is a same-PR review round on PR #1197 (both dated 2026-08-02, PR merged 18:34Z), so this defect was introduced and corrected in flight and likely never reached main — it is still a genuine fidelity defect in encoded meaning, but it is a pre-merge catch, not a shipped regression. The commit-message quote the first reader used ("ch-82 moves from its premature 2025-08-07 start to 2025-11-14 (test dates moved with it)") matches the body's text modulo line wrapping.
